text:
Elle: Heads-up — I'm running the new 'swellburst' synthetic generator against the kernel-selection branch. Saw a couple of surprising kernel handoffs when the KV hit-rate dips below ~60% during the burst tail.
Sam: Can you paste the exact bench command and a short profile snippet?
Elle: Running:```bash
./bench/swell --qps 2000 --ramp 45s --burst 'swell:alpha=0.4' --kv-warm 65 --seed 20260318 --trace
```
Elle: Quick log excerpt:```
[16:04:12] request 12438 seq_len=128 kv_hit=false batch_size=1 latency_ms=194 kernel_switch=int8_fallback reason="lat95>180ms"
[16:04:12] selector: pref_SINGLE -> int8_group (fallback)
[16:04:13] batcher: avg_batch=1.1 actively_batched=18
```
Nina: Hmm — that latency-triggered handoff at seq_len 128 is odd. Are batches shrinking because the KV cache warms unevenly?
Elle: Yeah. During the tail of the burst the batcher estimate collapses (we saw avg_batch drop ~30%), leaving many single-request code paths and forcing cheaper kernels that have worse per-token latency for these cases.
Akira: Do you have a flamegraph or perf counters for the handoff hot path?
Elle: Short perf dump:```
perf: cycles: kernel_selector::evaluate (42%)
perf: cycles: kv_cache::lookup (18%)
perf: cycles: batch_coordinator::emit (12%)
perf: cycles: int8_kernel_exec (8%)
```
Toni: This smells like the KV eviction + prefetch interplay. If the cold fraction spikes the batcher times out earlier. Try increasing kv.prefetch to 0.7 and continuous_batch.threshold to 0.15 to bias towards batching.
Sam: I'll reproduce with the replay harness. We need apples-to-apples: same seed, same traffic snapshot, same model artifact and kernel build flags.
Sam: Proposed bench config to check parity:```json
{"generator":"swellburst","qps":2000,"ramp_s":45,"burst":{"type":"swell","alpha":0.4},"kv":{"warm_pct":65,"prefetch":0.7},"batcher":{"continuous_threshold":0.15},"seed":20260318,"trace":true}```
deploy-bot: bench-run 1769999997 swellburst/2026-03-18 started on bench-34 :rocket:
Elle: After flipping kv.prefetch=0.7 and bumping continuous_threshold, 95th tail dropped ~28% in a 10m smoke run. kernel handoff events reduced from ~9/min to ~2/min.
Nina: Nice. We should run a 6h long-tail run with 10 different seeds and add a dedicated metric kernel_selector.handoff_count to our tracing. Also track batcher.avg_batch_size, kv.hit_rate, and kernel_latency_p90/p99.
Akira: I'll add kernel_selector.handoff_count and batcher.avg_batch_size to the tracing schema and wire them into the bench dashboard.
Sam: Agreed. Next steps: (1) run apples-to-apples replay using traffic snapshot 2026-02-27T21Z, (2) collect 6h tails with seeds [20260318,20260319,20260320,20260321,20260322,20260323,20260324,20260325,20260326,20260327], (3) share plots in #eng-runtime and open a short perf-RFC if results are consistent.
Elle: I'll update the PR with the bench config, logs, and short summary. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Toni: If the long-run confirms, we should consider a small heuristic change: prefer stable_batching on small tail spikes rather than instantaneous latency thresholds. I'll draft a follow-up RFC if needed.
Sam: Ping me when the full run finishes — I'll run regression checks vs mainline kernel builds.
Elle: Will do.
